questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘All the executive action of the Government of a state shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor’?

• **Article 166(1) **– States that all executive actions of a State Government shall be expressed in the name of the Governor.
 
• **Article 163(1) **– Specifies that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at the head to aid and advise the Governor in the exercise of his functions, except where the Governor is required to act at his discretion.
 
• **Article 164(1)** – Deals with the appointment of the Chief Minister and other ministers by the Governor and states that the ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the Governor.
 
• **Article 165(1)** – Provides for the appointment of the Advocate-General for the State by the Governor and mentions that he shall hold office during the pleasure of the Governor.

• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: A part of Rs. 48,500 is invested at a simple interest of 15% per annum. The rest of the money is invested at the rate of 10% simple interest per annum after 2 years of the first investment. The ratio of interest after 5 years from the time when the first amount was invested is 5 : 3. How much is the second part that was invested( in Rs.) at the rate of 10% simple interest?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Interest**: SI₁ : SI₂ = (P₁ × R₁ × T₁) : (P₂ × R₂ × T₂)

5 : 3 = (P₁ × 15 × 5) : (P₂ × 10 × 3) ⇒ 5/3 = (P₁ × 75) / (P₂ × 30)

P₁ / P₂ = (5 × 30) / (3 × 75) = 150 / 225 = 2 : 3

**Second Part** (P₂) = 48,500 × [3 / (2 + 3)] = 48,500 × 3/5 = 29,100

**∴ The correct answer is ₹29,100.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total Principal = **₹48,500**, Rate₁ = **15%**, Rate₂ = **10%**, Total Time = **5 years**.

**Formula Used:** Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d3510318092098364838ddf56b751add0ef790854f32feb85bfcff2a400b0c7.png] 

⇒ Let the first part be **P₁** and the second part be **P₂**.

⇒ Time for **P₁** = 5 years; Time for **P₂** = 5 − 2 = 3 years.

⇒ SI₁ = (P₁ × 15 × 5) / 100 = 75P₁ / 100

⇒ SI₂ = (P₂ × 10 × 3) / 100 = 30P₂ / 100

⇒ According to the question, SI₁ / SI₂ = 5 / 3

⇒ (75P₁ / 100) / (30P₂ / 100) = 5 / 3

⇒ 75P₁ / 30P₂ = 5 / 3

⇒ P₁ / P₂ = (5 × 30) / (3 × 75) = 150 / 225 = 2 / 3

⇒ P₂ = (3 / (2 + 3)) × 48,500 = (3/5) × 48,500

⇒ P₂ = 3 × 9,700 = 29,100

**∴ The correct answer is ₹29,100.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Principle

Simple interest is calculated only on the initial **Principal** amount. The formula is SI = (P × R × T) / 100.

Relative Time in Investment

When funds are invested at different starting times, the **Time (T)** for each part must be calculated relative to the final observation point (e.g., 5 years from the start).

Interest to Principal Ratio

The ratio of principals can be derived if the ratio of interests, rates, and time periods are known: P₁/P₂ = (SI₁/SI₂) × (R₂T₂ / R₁T₁).

questions.question: The value of (cosec θ - sin θ) (sec θ - cos θ) (tan θ + cot θ) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The value of (cosec θ - sin θ) (sec θ - cos θ) (tan θ + cot θ) is:

**Formula Used:**

We will use trigonometric identities to simplify the expression.

**Calculation:**

(cosec θ - sin θ) (sec θ - cos θ) (tan θ + cot θ)

Let us simplify each term separately:

cosec θ - sin θ = (1)/(sin θ) - sin θ

sec θ - cos θ = (1)/(cos θ) - cos θ

tan θ + cot θ = (sin θ)/(cos θ) + (cos θ)/(sin θ)

Combine them together:

⇒ ((1)/(sin θ) - sin θ) ((1)/(cos θ) - cos θ) ((sin θ)/(cos θ) + (cos θ)/(sin θ))

Simplify further:

⇒ ((1 - sin² θ)/(sin θ)) ((1 - cos² θ)/(cos θ)) ((sin² θ + cos² θ)/(sin θ cos θ))

Using the identity sin² θ + cos² θ = 1:

⇒ ((cos² θ)/(sin θ)) ((sin² θ)/(cos θ)) ((1)/(sin θ cos θ))

⇒ (cos² θ)/(sin θ) × (sin² θ)/(cos θ) × (1)/(sin θ cos θ)

⇒ (cos² θ × sin² θ)/(sin θ × cos θ × sin θ × cos θ)

⇒ (cos² θ × sin² θ)/(sin² θ × cos² θ)

⇒ 1

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.

options.text: I will be drive into town later on.
I will be driving into town later on.
I might drive into town later on.
I could be driving into town later on.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The direction of the question is **"Select the sentence that has a grammatical error."** and **option 1 is grammatically incorrect.**
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect verb form "**be drive**" instead of "**be driving**."
 
• In future continuous tense, the correct form is "**will be driving**."
 
• The correct phrase should be "**I will be driving into town later on**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I** will be driving** into town later on."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "I will be driving into town later on" – This sentence is grammatically** correct** and uses the correct form of the future continuous tense.
 
• **Option 3:** "I might drive into town later on" – This sentence is grammatically **correct** and uses the correct form of the modal verb "might".
 
• **Option 4:** "I could be driving into town later on" – This sentence is grammatically **correct **and uses the correct form of the modal verb "could" in the future continuous tense.
